subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — AvaHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kendra Morris <kendra@avahealth.com>
Cc: Samir Kapoor <samir@avahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — AvaHealth

Hi Kendra / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment and clear next steps.

Pain points you called out:
- Lack of unified observability: production prompt-level tracing is scattered across services and it's hard to correlate model calls to downstream metrics.
- No standard eval pipeline: QA runs are ad hoc, and you don't have "golden prompt" sets for regression detection.
- Rollout risk: limited ability to guard rollouts (no automatic regression alerts or traffic-split guardrails tied to quality metrics).

Current stack/environment:
- Inference: internal hybrid setup (in-house on-prem + cloud GPU) + vendor endpoints for burst capacity.
- Logging: mix of ELK and custom tracing; no integrated per-request KV/prompt tracing attached to model outputs.
- CI/Evals: unit tests + periodic manual evals in spreadsheets.

Success criteria you mentioned:
1) Prompt-level tracing that links user request -> model call -> downstream feature flags/metrics.
2) A repeatable eval pipeline with golden prompt sets and automated regression alerts.
3) Dashboarding for product + platform teams showing latency, cost/unit, and quality deltas by model version.

What Redwood can help with (high-level):
- Tracing hooks: lightweight SDK integration to capture request IDs and prompt/response payloads to our observability pipeline.
- Evals: managed eval runs with golden prompt sets, diff reports, and alerting on regression thresholds.
- Dashboards + rollouts: per-model dashboards and rollout guardrails (canary metrics, auto-fallback rules).

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share the obs requirements doc and the golden prompts template (attached).
2) Technical deep-dive with Dylan (runtime/observability) to scope SDK hooks and data retention. 30-45 min.
3) Pilot: run a 2-week eval against a subset of critical prompts + set up one dashboard and alert.

Can you confirm the people we should include on the technical call and a couple windows that work next week?

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Mobile: (415) 555-0198

Attachments: avahealth-observability-reqs.pdf, ava-golden-prompts.xlsx

From: Kendra Morris <kendra@avahealth.com>

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Observability & evals — AvaHealth

Thanks Marissa — this looks right and captures everything we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tracing: ideally the SDK can attach our internal request_id and patient_id (pseudonymized) as metadata so engineers can correlate model calls to downstream errors.
- Retention: legal wants logs retained for 90 days with role-based access; anything longer needs approval.
- Golden prompts: we have an initial set (~120 prompts) in a spreadsheet — I attached the current export. We'd like Redwood to suggest tiering (critical vs exploratory).

On participants for the technical deep-dive: please include Dylan (runtime), Neha (customer success/ops), and our platform eng lead Samir. Good windows next week: Mon 10-12 PST or Tue 13-15 PST.

Thanks — Kendra
Head of AI Products | AvaHealth
kendra@avahealth.com

Thanks Marissa — I can take the technical deep-dive. Quick notes before the call so we can be efficient:

1) Tracing hooks
- We'll provide a lightweight SDK that emits an envelope: {request_id, customer_id_hash, prompt_id, model_version, latency_ms} to our observability sink. (We’ll avoid storing raw PII by hashing customer ids.)
- Need to confirm authorization model for sending logs from their VPC vs our hosted pipeline.

2) Evals
- We can ingest their 120 prompts, suggest critical tiering (we'll flag top 30 based on business-critical intents), and run parallel evals across models.
- Regression alerts: configurable thresholds (default: 5% drop in top-line success rate) with slack/email notifications.

3) Dashboards & rollouts
- Canary metric set: latency, token-cost, pass-rate on golden prompts, and top-10 error clusters.
- Rollout guardrail: automatic rollback if canary pass-rate drops >5% for 10 minutes or error rate spikes above threshold.

I'll draft a short technical agenda and proposed checklist for the call today. Availability: Mon 10:30-11:30 PST works for me.

-Dylan
